title: Cobalt Bay deployment brief (client call scratch)
summary: Raw notes from 2024-11-07 kickoff with Cobalt Bay (regional grocery chain). They want an on-prem/private deployment for PII-sensitive search+assistant; main asks: sub-200ms tail latency for queries that hit KG augmentation, per-request cost predictability, HA across two data centers, and a simple rollback for model regressions. Client is cautious about full internet egress and needs formal network diagram before we start staging.
call_notes: Attendees: Andy Mercer (CIO), Priya Rao (Lead ML infra), Evan (app lead), Maya (Redwood CS), Liam (SE). Quick intro -> scope: deploy assistant for store staff (inventory lookup, shift scheduling help, SOP retrieval). They have 2 DCs (west/east) — prefer active/standby with failover window < 60s. Data: product catalog + internal SOPs (sensitive customer PII in logs). Priya emphasized no raw logs leaving the VPC. They asked about KMS integration and HSM for key storage. Evan wants near-realtime sync for catalog updates (sub-5s). They will provide a VPN to our private control plane + network peering. Andy asked about upgrade rollbacks and whether can pin a model to older weights per-route.
requirements:
- Deployment: Private (VPC) or on-prem appliance behind customer firewall.
- Throughput: ~120 QPS peak (store queries), burst to 300 for promos.
- Latency target: median <60ms, p95 <180ms for short prompts (<256 tokens).
- Data residency: No customer logs exported. Must integrate with customer KMS/HSM.
- Model policy: ability to pin to model version and auto-fallback to a lighter quantized variant.
- Sync: catalog update window <5s end-to-end.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route SLIs, 30d retention for traces (min), alerts for quality regressions.
- Compliance: SOC2 + region-specific privacy review (they mentioned Alberta PIPA)
- SLA ask: 99.9% uptime for production route; can offer dedicated pool or reserved capacity.
- Ops: prefer canary deploys with traffic-split by store id, and instant abort on model regression.
technical_gotchas:
- Catalog sync: they use Kafka topics; need to validate idempotency and compaction so partial replays don't create duplicates.
- KV cache: with frequent small queries, caching prefixes may be less effective; need to prototype prefix/KV TTLs per-store.
- Quantized variant: some of their SOP prompts include long code-like snippets -> INT8/q8 fallback might lose accuracy. Must run evals on their prompt set.
- Network: their firewall blocks ephemeral high-port ranges currently; our private agent will need specific egress ports whitelisted (list to follow).
- Observability: they want token cost attribution on per-store basis; invoice mapping requires store_id propagated in request headers.
- HA: their active/standby DCs are separated by 150ms network — cross-DC KV replication could increase tail latency; consider async replication + fast failover policy.
- Data handling: they require that PII be redacted before any debug logs leave the cluster; build a redaction hook in the control plane.
open_questions:
1) Will Cobalt Bay provide a dedicated VLAN for the Redwood runtime nodes, or do we run within their shared subnet?
2) Which KMS/HSM vendor and API versions are they on (AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault, Thales HSM?)
3) Expected model family: do they want open Llama-family weights, or are they considering closed LLMs? (affects licensing + quantization options)
4) Confirm retention windows for traces and logs — 30d nominal, but legal may require longer.
5) Who is the internal approver for network changes (name/email) to speed up firewall rules?

quick_config_sketch: Staging suggestion: Dedicated pool w/ autoscale cap 300 qps, batch target 16 tokens, prefix cache TTL 120s (tune after eval). Model variant mapping: cbay-v1 (float16) -> cbay-v1-q4_0 (quantized) as fallback. Enable request header x-store-id to propagate for cost attribution. Use async KV replication cross-DC, with fast-failover route to standby when p95 CPU > 85% for 30s.
